headlines: STUDY FINDS AT LEAST 35 MIAMI BARRIER ISLAND HIGH-RISES ARE SINKING UNEVENLY
MIAMI LUXURY TOWERS ARE TILTING AND SINKING INTO THE GROUND
COULD LUXURY TOWERS ON OUR COAST BE FACING HIDDEN STRUCTURAL DAMAGE?
draft.article: New research from University of Miami professor Falk Amelung reveals that at least 35 high-rises along our barrier islands are sinking unevenly into the earth. The 2024 study examined prominent properties, including the Porsche Design Tower, the Faena Hotel, and towers named after Donald Trump. While massive structures normally stop settling shortly after completion, these coastal buildings continue to sink years later into the underlying sand and porous limestone. Engineers warn that this uneven sinking, known as differential settlement, causes towers to tilt and internally deform. Over time, these shifts could bring severe structural damage along with surging insurance and maintenance expenses across Miami-Dade.
